chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Mutawakkil (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ibrahim al-Kharasani (al-Karkhi), who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him):

'My female companion died and she was agreeable with me, and I have considered marrying.' He said: 'Look to where you place yourself, and who you share your property with, and make observe your religion, your secret, and your trust. If you must do so, then marry a virgin who is ascribed to goodness and good character.'

'Indeed, women are created diverse: among them is the one who is a gain and a love; among them is the one like the crescent moon when it shines to its companion; and among them are those of darkness. Whoever acquires a good one will be happy, and whoever is defrauded will have no revenge. They are three: a fertile, affectionate woman who assists her husband in his lifetime for his worldly and afterlife affairs, and does not assist the world against him; a barren woman, without beauty or character, who does not assist her husband in goodness; and a noisy, restless, slandering woman who considers much to be little and does not accept the simple.'
ai.seo_question: What are the three types of women described in Shia hadith and how to choose the best wife?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) guides Ibrahim al-Karkhi on the prudence of remarriage, prioritizing a virgin of good lineage and character to safeguard one's wealth, property, and spiritual secrets. The Imam categorizes women into three archetypes—beneficial and affectionate, barren and lacking virtue, and noisy and slandering—highlighting the practical and spiritual implications of each type on a husband's worldly and otherworldly success. This classification reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on *khuluq* (character) and *nasab* (lineage) as key criteria for marital compatibility.
